ideas.hypothesis: Exact-cover dynamic programming on symbol subsets and uncovered negatives counts all compatible ownerships without listing every Bell partition.
ideas.purpose: Broaden usable exact identification beyond the sufficient graph r=k test; no polynomial complexity claim.

ideas.hypothesis: A trusted allowed count set can certify ownership without an exact trusted k; constraints may eliminate all but one count and partition.
ideas.candidate: Doubled-pairs abcdef with P={epsilon,aabb,ccdd,eeff}, N={bbaa,ddcc,ffee}, allowed_k=[3,4].
ideas.boundary: The allowed set must contain the true count by external assumption; it is not invented from the sample.

ideas.hypothesis: Exact pair coownership counts certify partial ownership even when the whole partition is ambiguous.
ideas.candidate: abcd with P={abcd}, N={bacd}, allowed_k=[2]: a,b forced together while other pairs may remain ambiguous.
ideas.boundary: No universal pair claims on an empty version space or incomplete DP.

not_claimed: no-state-bound prime-factor inference from finite traces
